long_biography.plain_text:
Cirque du Soleil grew from a 1984 Quebec government-backed touring show into one of the world's largest live-entertainment companies. Guy Laliberté, an accordionist, stilt-walker and fire-eater who had performed with Baie-Saint-Paul street artists, named the troupe and guided its synthesis of circus, theatre, music and design. Its international expansion made him a billionaire; he sold most of his holding to outside investors and disposed of the remaining 10% in 2020.

At Lune Rouge, Laliberté remains founder and chief executive of a platform spanning entertainment, technology and real-estate projects. He also created One Drop to support sustainable access to safe water, and used his trip to the International Space Station to draw attention to water issues. Across these ventures, his recurring approach has been to combine spectacle, entrepreneurship and social purpose.
